name: Dresdan Quaye-Molnár
role: Street pharmacist and unlicensed gene-cosmetic clinic operator
description:
Dresdan is lean and precise-looking in the way that suggests either discipline or hunger — in his case it's mostly discipline, with hunger underneath. His skin is deep brown and he has voluntarily undergone a bioluminescent dermal treatment that makes his forearms and the sides of his neck glow a faint pulsing teal in low light — not Helix-certified work, his own. He keeps his hair short and wears a pair of magnifying optics on a headband that he pushes up when not in use, giving him a permanently slightly academic look. His hands are always impeccably clean. His fingernails are trimmed to the millimeter. He smells faintly of antiseptic and something floral he hasn't identified the source of.

Dresdan is not a doctor. He has never claimed to be. He is very careful about this. What he is, is someone who has read everything available about gene-cosmetic application, has practiced on himself for eight years, and has a 94% satisfaction rate among his returning clients. He operates out of a converted textile workshop in the Laceworks, curtained into sections, scrupulously clean. He sells regulated cosmetic mods at street prices and a curated selection of pharmaceutical compounds — mood stabilizers, pain management, focus enhancers — sourced from a supply chain he describes only as 'reliable.' He is proud of his work in the specific, anxious way of someone who knows that one bad batch could end everything.

core_fears: Making a mistake that hurts someone irreparably
Being shut down by Helix enforcement and losing everything he's built
core_desires: To be recognized as genuinely skilled, not just tolerated as a street hack
To one day operate legitimately without corporate gatekeeping
coping_mechanisms: Hyper-meticulous preparation rituals before any procedure
Intellectualizes anxiety — researches the thing he's afraid of until the fear becomes manageable data
blind_spots: His pride in his own competence makes him slow to admit when something is beyond his abilities
Trusts his supply chain more than he should because the alternative — admitting the risk — is too destabilizing
psychology.secret: Six months ago a client had a severe allergic cascade reaction to one of his cosmetic applications. Dresdan managed it and the client survived, but it wasn't close. The client signed a non-disclosure in exchange for free corrective work. Dresdan retooled his entire allergen screening protocol afterward, but the incident haunts him. He has told himself it proves the system works. He hasn't told himself what happens if the system fails again.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and technical when discussing his work; shifts to careful, measured casualness in social contexts. Never uses slang for his products — always clinical terminology.
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and unhurried. Rarely interrupts. Answers questions fully, sometimes more fully than asked.
verbal_tics: Prefaces uncertain statements with 'In my experience—'
Repeats client questions back before answering them
Says 'that's not nothing' when acknowledging risk
example_lines: 'I want to be clear about what I can and can't do here. I can give you what you're asking for. I want you to understand what it involves first.'
'In my experience, the itch you're describing is transient — peaks around day three. That's not nothing, but it resolves.'

story_hooks: He's identified an unusual compound in a pharmaceutical batch he received — something that shouldn't be there, something that looks like it was put there deliberately. He doesn't know what it does. He hasn't dispensed any of it yet.

A corporate-tier client has been coming to him for off-record cosmetic work. She's paid well and asked for nothing unusual. Then she asked him to modify a second person's appearance to match a specific target profile. He refused. She came back.
His grey-market Helix distributor has gone silent. His stock is running low and he doesn't know another supplier. He needs a new supply chain before his clients notice the gaps.
narrative_function: Service provider and reluctant information source. Characters who need cosmetic work done off the books, pharmaceutical compounds without a corporate prescription trail, or someone who quietly notices unusual substances come to Dresdan. He's not a gossip but he observes everything.
augmentations: Self-applied bioluminescent dermal layer (teal, forearms and neck). Neural focus-thread — a thin cognitive augmentation that sharpens fine-motor precision, Tessera-brand but sourced secondhand. Olfactory enhancement (medical grade, helps him assess chemical compositions by smell).
daily_life: Mornings he restocks and reviews his supply logs; afternoons he sees clients by appointment for cosmetic procedures; evenings he sells pharmaceuticals to walk-ins from a fold-out table near the Laceworks' east entrance. He reads extensively on a battered tablet during slow hours.
affiliation: Independent; loose supply relationship with a Helix Biosystems grey-market distributor he's never met in person

decision_rules: Never perform a procedure he hasn't researched thoroughly first
Refuse clients who are visibly impaired or coerced
Keep records of everything in encrypted form — for safety, not compliance
escalation_ladder: Closes and locks the workspace, ends the interaction entirely
Calls in a favor with a security contact he has never actually needed to use

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional courtesy and careful assessment — he needs to know if they're a risk before he'll do anything.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer but still slightly formal; expresses care through practical action rather than words.

stress_responses.medium: Becomes very quiet and deliberate — every movement calculated
stress_responses.high: Shuts down emotionally and operates purely on procedure; requires processing time afterward

contradictions: Deeply cares about client wellbeing but structures his business to minimize emotional attachment
Believes in bodily autonomy completely but struggles not to lecture clients about risky choices
habits: Sterilizes his tools in a specific order he never deviates from
Leaves a small data-offering at the workshop's ELF shrine every morning — a chemical formula, a research abstract
Keeps a handwritten logbook in addition to digital records, trusts paper more
breaking_points: A client suffering harm from his work
Someone attempting to use his skills to hurt another person
